purpose: Supplementary exploration of K4 (b): whether the growth exponent of the amplitude-weighted frequency centroid of the two-dimensional sum field approaches the estimate e(gamma) = min(1, 1.5 - 1/gamma) as N grows. Three approaches: (1) direct computation extended to N = 8192 and 16384; (2) extrapolation of the local slopes with forms fixed below; (3) an estimate (not a proof) of the leading terms of the centroid, compared with the computed shell spectrum and the approach of the local slopes.
status: Exploratory. Designed on 2026-10-26 after the results of K4 (results/k4_centroid_2d.json and .md, commit cb369b4) had been seen, in particular the local slopes that increase with N in every cell. It is not blind and is not used as evidence for the claims of the main text: the slopes over the finite N ranges of Appendix B and the rejection of the estimate rest on K4 alone. Its results belong to the supplement and are reported as exploratory.
fixed_before_running: Written before any computation in this file. A timing run on seed 901 (outside the seeds below) at N = 8192, 16384 and 32768 was used only to estimate the computational cost and memory; its centroid values were not printed or used. Any change after this commit increases the version, is listed under 'deviations' with its reason, and is added to the history of INDEX.json.
cells: The 12 cells of the rejection criterion of k4_centroid_2d.json: field = sum (S1.2, four octaves, maxabs normalisation S1.4), f in {3, 5, 7}, gamma in {0.9, 1.25, 1.75, 2.6}, processing = raw (no window), descriptor = centroid_amp (S2.3), direct sampling.
seeds_note: The seeds of K4, so that every seed's series extends the K4 series of the same field.
grids_note: Every N is recomputed with the implementation below; N = 128-4096 also serve as the implementation check. N = 32768 is not included: the timing run showed memory compression on the 16 GB machine used, so it is not computed in this file.
height: H = T_gamma(F) with s = 1 (s does not affect the centroid; S2.2).

implementation.rule: The centroid of S2.3 computed without holding the full complex two-dimensional DFT. F is built by row blocks as in procedural_field_separable (same draws and order of operations); max |F| over the grid is found in a first pass and F is divided by it (maxabs, S1.4); H = T_gamma(F) is transformed along rows with a real FFT (bins kx = 0 ... N/2), then along columns by column blocks. Both sums of S2.3 are accumulated over the half plane with weight 2 for 0 < kx < N/2 and weight 1 for kx = 0 and kx = N/2 (|H^(-k)| = |H^(k)| for real H; the bin kx = -N/2 of fftfreq is the bin kx = N/2 of the real FFT, with the same rho). The DC bin is set to 0 instead of subtracting the mean of H: the DFT of H - mean(H) equals the DFT of H at every k != 0 and is 0 at k = 0, so the quantity is that of S2.3; only the rounding differs.
implementation.check: Implementation control, not a finding: for every cell, seed and N in 128-4096 the value must agree with the centroid_amp of the raw processing (direct sampling, r = 1, maxabs) stored in results/k4_centroid_2d.json (commit cb369b4, SHA-256 257173c1b375595146a4f23a746fb8e2d8537a6df6426eeb1c82b40d37f6872a) to a relative difference of at most 1e-9. A missing, non-finite or non-positive value counts as a disagreement. If any value disagrees, the run is stopped before any N > 4096 is computed and nothing else is reported until the cause is found.
implementation.finite_values: Every computed centroid and shell density must be finite (and the centroid positive); otherwise the run stops. An interval that is not finite gives the outcome 'not determined'.
implementation.resume: An interrupted run may be resumed from its partial file only if the partial file was written with the same condition file, specification, reference file, script and library versions (recorded in its first line); otherwise the run refuses to resume.
implementation.shell_spectrum: From the same pass: for logarithmic shells with edges rho = 2^(j/8) (j = 0, 1, ...; the last shell is cut at the largest rho of the grid), the sum over the bins of the shell of |H^_k| / N^2, divided by the width of the shell (the shell density). Stored for every N.

readouts: Seed means and standard errors of the centroid at every N.
Local slopes between consecutive N (mean and standard error over seeds), extending those of K4 by 4096-8192 and 8192-16384.

Slopes over N 2048-16384 (four points) and N 4096-16384 (three points): mean and simultaneous interval over seeds (Bonferroni, level 1 - 0.05/12, t with 19 degrees of freedom), and whether the interval contains e(gamma), lies below or above it. This is a description over a larger finite range, not a repetition of the rejection criterion of K4.

approach_2_extrapolation.local_slope_points: Per seed, the local slopes s_j between consecutive N with N >= 512 (512-1024, ..., 8192-16384: five values), each placed at the geometric mean N_j of its two grids.

forms.name: E1
forms.rule: Per seed, nonlinear least squares of ln C_N = ln(a + b N^c) over N 512-16384 (six points), with a > -min(C_N), b > 0 and 0 < c <= 1.5, started from c = the last local slope. The extrapolated exponent is c. A seed's fit is counted as failed if it does not converge, if c ends at a bound, if the growing term b N^c changes the model over the range by less than 1e-6 of the largest C_N (then c is not identified; this includes b at its lower bound), if a ends at its lower bound, or if the fitted a + b N^c is not finite and positive at every N of the range. If more than 2 of the 20 seeds fail in a cell, E1 is 'not determined' for that cell; otherwise the interval is over the seeds that did not fail (conditional on that selection), and the number of failed seeds is reported.

forms.name: E2
forms.rule: Per seed, linear least squares of s_j = s_inf + d / ln N_j over the five local slopes. The extrapolated exponent is s_inf.

forms.name: E3
forms.rule: Per seed, linear least squares of s_j = s_inf + d N_j^(-delta(gamma)) over the five local slopes, with delta(gamma) fixed by the estimate of approach 3 (exactly 7/18, 3/10, 1/14 and 3/26, that is 0.3889, 0.3, 0.0714 and 0.1154 at gamma = 0.9, 1.25, 1.75 and 2.6). The extrapolated exponent is s_inf; d may have either sign.

approach_2_extrapolation.sensitivity: The same three forms on N 1024-16384 (E1: five points; E2 and E3: the four local slopes from 1024-2048 on).
approach_2_extrapolation.intervals: Mean of the extrapolated exponent over seeds and simultaneous t interval (Bonferroni, level 1 - 0.05/12) for each form and range. The adjustment is over the 12 cells of one form and one range, not over all forms, ranges and readouts together. Intervals over seeds do not include the error of extrapolating a form beyond the data or the misspecification of the form.
approach_2_extrapolation.outcome: For each cell, form and range: 'contains e(gamma)', 'below' or 'above'. All three are reported as results; none is a decision about the conjecture. Disagreements between forms and between ranges are reported as the dependence of the extrapolation on its form.
approach_2_extrapolation.note: The forms differ in what they assume about the approach (E1: one growing power over a constant, E2: a logarithmic correction, E3: the rate of approach 3). The extrapolated values are not limits; they are reported to show how far apart reasonable extrapolations are.

approach_3_estimate.status: An estimate, not a proof. Its content is limited to what is written here; it was written before the computation and is not extended after the results are seen (time limit). Not treated: the contribution of inflection points of the zero lines, aliasing of the DFT near N/2, and the form of the low-frequency part.
assumptions: With alpha = 1/gamma, near its zero lines (smooth closed or periodic curves for the sum field) H behaves like sign(d) |d|^alpha times a smooth factor, d the signed distance to the line.

For a curved line, the two-dimensional Fourier coefficient of such a singularity decays like |k|^-(alpha + 3/2) on average over directions (decay alpha + 1 across the line, and 1/2 from stationary phase along it), so that the shell density S(rho) behaves like A rho^-(alpha + 1/2) for large rho.
The rest of the spectrum (the octave components and their combinations at low rho) contributes finite constants P (numerator) and D (denominator) that do not grow with N.

The next term of S(rho) is smaller than A rho^-(alpha + 1/2) by a factor rho^-eta with eta > delta(gamma), so that it does not change the orders below. Without this, the leading behaviour A rho^-(alpha + 1/2) (1 + o(1)) allows slower corrections and the orders below are not determined.
derivation: With the DFT coefficients approximated by the Fourier coefficients up to rho of order N, the numerator of S2.3 is P + A' N^(3/2 - alpha) (1 + o(1)) with A' > 0. The constant P (the low-frequency sum minus the lower end of the integral of the asymptotic term) can have either sign. For alpha > 1/2 (gamma < 2) the denominator is a convergent sum, D - B N^-(alpha - 1/2) with D, B > 0 (the omitted tail is positive). For alpha < 1/2 (gamma > 2) the denominator is D' + B N^(1/2 - alpha) with B > 0 and D' of either sign.
Hence C_N grows like N^(3/2 - alpha) for gamma < 2 and like N for gamma > 2, which is e(gamma).

The local slope s(N) = d ln C_N / d ln N is the slope of the numerator minus the slope of the denominator. For gamma < 2 the numerator gives a correction of order N^-(3/2 - alpha) of undetermined sign, and the denominator a correction of order N^-(alpha - 1/2) that makes s(N) smaller than e(gamma). The correction is of order N^-delta with delta(gamma) = min(3/2 - alpha, alpha - 1/2): 0.3889 at gamma = 0.9 (numerator term; the sign is not determined by the estimate), 0.3 at 1.25 and 0.0714 at 1.75 (denominator term; the local slope approaches e(gamma) from below).

For gamma > 2 the leading correction comes from the constant D' of the denominator, of order N^-(1/2 - alpha), with delta = 1/2 - alpha = 0.1154 at gamma = 2.6 and a sign that the estimate does not determine; the correction of the numerator, of order N^-(3/2 - alpha), is smaller.

The small delta at gamma = 1.75 and 2.6 means that, if the assumptions hold, an existing deficit d at N_j shrinks only by the factor 4^-delta (0.91 at gamma = 1.75, 0.85 at gamma = 2.6) for every factor 4 in N. How large the deficit is depends on constants that the estimate does not give.
compared_quantities: Shell exponent: per seed, least-squares slope of ln S(rho) on ln rho over the shells with 512 <= rho < 2048 (16 shells) at N = 16384; mean and simultaneous interval over seeds (Bonferroni, level 1 - 0.05/12), compared with -(alpha + 1/2): -1.6111, -1.3, -1.0714 and -0.8846 at gamma = 0.9, 1.25, 1.75 and 2.6. The same band at N = 8192 is reported beside it, with the difference of the seed means between the two grids (no interval). The difference reflects how the aliasing and the other grid effects change between the two grids, not their absolute size; agreement does not exclude a bias common to both.

Rate of approach: per seed, the least-squares slope of ln(e(gamma) - s_j) on ln N_j over the five local slopes from 512 on (computed only for seeds whose five deficits are all positive; the number of such seeds is reported; the interval is conditional on that selection and needs at least 2 such seeds), mean and 95% t interval over those seeds, compared with -delta(gamma). The sign of e(gamma) - s_j at every j is reported for every cell.

predictions: P-S1 (approach 1): in every one of the 12 cells, the mean local slope 4096-8192 is larger than the mean local slope 2048-4096, and the mean local slope 8192-16384 is larger than the mean local slope 4096-8192.
P-S2 (approach 1): in every one of the 12 cells, the simultaneous interval of the slope over N 4096-16384 lies entirely below e(gamma).
P-S3 (approach 2): no direction is predicted. For each cell, form and range the outcome ('contains e(gamma)', 'below', 'above' or 'not determined') is reported.
P-S4 (approach 3, the assumption on the shell density): in every one of the 12 cells, the simultaneous interval of the shell exponent at N = 16384 contains a value within 0.05 of -(alpha + 1/2).

P-S5 (approach 3, the rate of approach): in every one of the 12 cells, the five deficits e(gamma) - s_j are positive in all 20 seeds, their seed means decrease with N, and the 95% interval of the fitted rate contains -delta(gamma). (The positive sign is implied by the estimate only at gamma = 1.25 and 1.75; at gamma = 0.9 and 2.6 it is expected from the local slopes of K4.)
operational_notes: The 'larger than' of P-S1 compares seed means without a tolerance. In P-S4 'contains a value within 0.05' means that the interval intersects [-(alpha + 1/2) - 0.05, -(alpha + 1/2) + 0.05]; a wider interval satisfies it more easily, so the interval widths are reported beside it, and P-S4 is not a statement about the precision of the exponent.
not_done: N = 32768 and above. Other fields (product1, oned), non-integer f, the Hann window and the power-weighted centroids. Verification of the zero-line geometry (inflection points). A proof.
deviations_before_running: 2026-10-26, before any computation: revised after independent checks (Codex and a code review of the script). Changes: an assumption on the next term of the shell density in approach 3 and a narrower wording of what a small delta implies; the reference SHA-256 and the treatment of missing or non-finite values in the implementation check; the finite-value and resume rules; further failure cases of E1; the meaning of the Bonferroni adjustment, of intervals over selected seeds and of the difference between the two grids; exact values of delta(gamma).
